newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MARK FEELS LIKE FISH OUT OF WATER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARK FEELS LIKE FISH OUT OF WATER.

text.p: South African defender Mark Fish, who was courted by Manchester United before signing for Lazio in the close season, is feeling rather washed up in the Italian first division.

Fish has played in only two competitive matches and is being kept out by Alessandro Nesta and Argentine Jose Chamot, who appear to be Czech coach Zedenek Zeman's first choice central defensive pairing.

Although Lazio paid South Africa's Orlando Pirates $1.3 million for him, Fish has only started for Lazio in their opening day 2-0 defeat by Bologna -- when he was substituted five minutes from time. His only other appearance was in the club's 1-0 Italian Cup win against third division Avellino.
Fish said on Thursday: "Nesta and Chamot are very good players. Italy has a very important championship and I'm still a young player, just 22 years old and I'm here to learn, but...
"Perhaps my style, my game isn't suited to Lazio."

Fish was the outstanding player in South Africa's African Nations' Cup win earlier this year. As well as attracting interest from Manchester United, Everton and French club Bordeaux were also impressed by him before he moved to Italy.
